newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan VP approves state share sales to citizens.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan VP approves state share sales to citizens.

text.p: Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan has approved a cabinet plan to sell up to 30 percent of each of three major state enterprises to the island's citizens, local newspapers reported on Sunday.

The plan, first proposed by the cabinet on January 17, would allow Taiwan citizens to buy stakes in Chinese Petroleum Corp, Taiwan Power Co, and Chunghwa Telecom -- state firms with a combined net worth of T$1.066 trillion (US$38.85 billion).
"The plan will enable the people to share the benefits of the fruits of state-run enterprises," Lien was quoted by the China Times newspaper as saying.

Under the plan, each of the 14 million adult citizens of Taiwan would be eligible to purchase stakes in the three state firms through a system of preferential treatement aimed at preventing concentrated buying by conglomerates.
Adults, defined as being at least 19 years old, could be buy up to 3,000 shares each, according to the proposal.
The plan, devised by the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development, would be implemented over a period of time to minimize the impact on the island's capital markets.
The cabinet had said that Chinese Petroleum, with a net value of T$261 billion, would sell stakes in the firm as early as July, followed by T$478 billion Taiwan Power and T$326 billion Chunghwa.
In previous Taiwanese privatisations, local media and analysts complained that certain private conglomerates had managed to take control of some firms, and called this a breach of government trust.
Their calls for the government to reform its privatisation procedures resulted in the new scheme.
Privatisation of the three firms could help reduce the government's budget deficit, officials have said.
The government, dogged by a shortfall in tax revenue amid a slow economy n the first three quarters of 1996, has forecast a fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) deficit of T$87.6 billion.
